Risk: Myopic behavior in artificial agents
Problem analysis: Stratified credit assignment architecture separating epistemic and instrumental modules
Theoretical insight: External gradient sources are required for learning to act online
Design rationale: Unified credit assignment across prediction and action to reduce myopia
Design rationale: Use actor-critic framework to approximate gradients via learned value estimates
Implementation mechanism: Policy gradient update using critic baseline
Validation evidence: Improved learning stability observed in actor-critic algorithms in RL benchmarks
Intervention: Train actor-critic RL agents with critic baseline during fine-tuning to mitigate myopia
